title: Creative Inspiration
summary: Students identify inspiration sources, connect them to visible design choices and mood, read and hear short inspiration notes, and produce one scaffolded inspiration-note card.
essential_question: How can I explain what inspired a design and why I chose its main visual elements in simple English?
professional_context: Week 12 connects English to early concept development, inspiration-board discussion, sketch rationale, and portfolio-ready explanation language. Students move from describing visible features to explaining where a design idea comes from and what effect the main design choices create.
language_focus: inspiration-source nouns such as inspiration, source, reference, theme, and idea
common inspiration areas such as nature, city, street style, music, art, architecture, history, memory, and movement
mood and effect language such as calm, bold, playful, elegant, soft, strong, and modern
design-choice verbs such as choose, use, combine, and add
fixed rationale frames such as This design is inspired by ..., The colors come from ..., and I chose ... because ...
teacher_preparation: Preview the opener board, the inspiration-source board, the mood-and-effect board, and the reusable image A to image D gallery before class.
Keep visible sentence frames for This design is inspired by ..., The colors come from ..., I chose ... because ..., This creates ..., and The overall look is ....
Keep the main writing task line-based and scaffolded. Do not turn the Design Inspiration Note Card into a paragraph or add a word-count target.
Check that the Week 12 reusable image A to image D gallery, the numbered listening script, the question labels, the options, and the correct answers all match exactly before using the listening task.
Prepare quick correction support for inspired by, because clauses, article use, and source-to-design links such as The colors come from ....
Decide whether students will use projected inspiration images, printed gallery cards, or teacher-selected visual references during the speaking session.
student_deliverables: Completion of the Week 12 opener selections.
Completion of the main inspiration-source matching set.
Completion of the main mood-and-visual-effect matching set.
Reading-comprehension responses matching four inspiration notes to image A, image B, image C, or image D and answering detail questions.
Listening-comprehension responses identifying inspiration sources, design choices, and moods from one short numbered listening clip.
Completion of five rationale phrase-practice fill blanks.
A scaffolded Design Inspiration Note Card with 6 required sentence-frame lines and 1 optional challenge line.
Two corrected Week 12 design-rationale sentences saved after review.
A short teacher-observed oral explanation of one inspiration source and one design choice.
